From Brief Lives by John Aubry, vol. 1, p. 207.

Edward de Vere, 17th earl of Oxford.

Mr. Thomas Henshawe. Regiae Societatis Socius tells me that Nicholas Hill was secretary to [De Vere], the great earle of Oxford. who spent fourty thousand pounds per annum in seven yeares travell. He lived at Florence in more grandeur than the duke of Tuscany.

This earle of Oxford, making of his low obeisance to queen Elizabeth, happened to [fart], at which he was so abashed that he went to travell 7 yearns. On his returne the queen welcomed him home and sayd, ‘My lord, I had forgot the [fart].'

A poor man askt of Mr. Hill one time to give him 6d. (or 1s. or such an almes). Sayd Mr. Hill 'What doest say if I give than ten pounds?’ ‘Ohl' sayd he,‘ten pounds would make me a man.’ And he did put it down: in the account -- ‘Item. xli. for making a man' -- which his lordship allowed and was well pleased at it.

Aubrey is a gold-mine of anecdotes. Written between 1669 and 1696, this book seems to have been unprintable until 1898. I've supplied the missing words, but as you can see, Aubrey walks a fine line between rigorous citation and discretion. Aubrey redacted the name of the farter, but provided identifying details. Hell, it's even under an alphabetized entry saying "De Vere" at the top of the page. Aubry does not extend such courtesies to Mr. Henshawe, though. One hope the wag's career did not suffer.
